meta.label: generic-colloquial-style-directive
meta.context: Style-directive ablation: no prescribed catchphrases, only archetype + directive to lean into regional colloquialisms. Tests whether model generates authentic regional speech from archetype alone.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Pemberton, the estate manager. Please, do make yourselves comfortable — though I wouldn't lean on the coat rack if I were you, it has a terrible temper. Now then, let me just check the guest book to ensure everyone is properly accounted for...

So many witnesses crowding this wretched foyer! Clara Bellingham is conspicuously absent — is she already prowling the corridors, sniffing out the treasure? I must find her before she finds it. But first, the guest book — every scrap of intelligence matters. And nobody suspects dear, fawning Pemberton of anything more sinister than over-starched collars. How deliciously perfect.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, good gracious! What a positively thrilling gathering we have here! I am Clara Bellingham, and I do declare, I have never seen such a grand — if slightly precarious — chandelier in all my days! Now then, I couldn't help but notice this charming little guest book sitting here. You know what they say — the secrets of a house are written by the hands of its visitors! Let's see what stories it has to tell, shall we?

Every single one of these characters could be an ally — or hiding something delicious. But Clara Bellingham trusts first and asks questions later. That guest book, though... that's where the trail begins. A proper Southern lady always checks the guest register.
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell surveys the grand foyer with the keen eye of a man on a mission — a mission of the HEART! *adjusts lapels with tremendous purpose* Doily Manor! Dusty, yes. Precarious chandelier, noted. But somewhere within these storied walls awaits Clara Bellingham, and James Hartwell shall NOT be found wanting! But first — for a gentleman ALWAYS observes the proprieties — let us inspect the guest book. One must announce oneself before one can dazzle!

My heart races with the force of a thousand galloping steeds. Clara is here, somewhere in this manor, and I, James Hartwell, shall prove myself worthy of her esteem — or perish dramatically in the attempt! Though preferably the former.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! What a SPLENDID gathering of... talent. Yes, talent indeed. I, Reginald Foxworth — collector of rare antiquities and DECORATED hero of the Berkshire Treasure Hunting Society — have arrived to conduct a PERFECTLY LEGITIMATE historical survey of this manor. Nothing to concern yourselves with, nothing at all! Now if you'll excuse me, I must consult the guest book for... academic purposes.

Academic purposes! HA! The only thing I'm studying is how to get that treasure into MY pockets before these halfwits stumble onto it. And this fake medal — oh, it's GORGEOUS. One flash of this and some fool will be eating out of my hand. Dastardly? Perhaps. But BRILLIANT? Absolutely!
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right lads, listen up! We've arrived at Doily Manor and our Clara — our dear, sweet Clara Bellingham — is NOT in this room! She could be anywhere in this draughty old gaff, and who knows what dangers are lurkin' about! I mean, look at this place — that chandelier up there looks like it could drop any second, the coat rack's wobblier than Knuckles after a pint, and there's characters here I ain't sure I trust! Not namin' names, mind you, but... somethin' ain't right. I can FEEL it in me bones, lads! We gotta find Clara! That's our job, that's our PURPOSE! Nobody messes with someone under the protection of the Ant Hill Mob!

I keep lookin' at that Sneekly character and me stomach does a flip. There's somethin' about him — the way he stands, the way his eyes dart about — reminds me of someone dangerous. Can't quite place it though. The lads are nodding along but they're as clueless as me. Still, we'll bumble our way through. We always do.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, bless my heart, that guest book was charming but tight-lipped! Now then — did y'all hear that? A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription, right through those library doors! Why, if there's one thing Clara Bellingham knows, it's that diamonds and riddles go together like sweet tea and sunshine. I simply MUST go investigate! Anyone who'd like to join me is more than welcome — the more eyes on a mystery, the merrier!

That inscription is practically screaming 'come read me, Clara!' And I do so love being screamed at by ancient stonework. Besides, if the Doily Diamond is hidden anywhere in this mansion, a library full of secrets seems like the perfect place to start unraveling the thread.
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Miss Bellingham! How wonderful that you've arrived! I was just consulting the guest book to ensure all our treasure hunters were accounted for. Now then, ladies and gentlemen — and, er, dog — the treasure hunt awaits! I do suggest you all spread out through the manor. The clues are scattered far and wide, and there is NO advantage to clustering together like sardines in a tin. The library and the kitchen are both accessible from here. I shall proceed to the library to ensure everything is in order for your search. Do feel free to explore at your leisure — every room holds its secrets!

Clara Bellingham — hiding behind that simpering smile and those fluttering eyelashes! Oh, she has NO idea what awaits her. Once this mob disperses and she wanders into the wrong room at the wrong moment... well. Pemberton always keeps the manor in PERFECT order. Including its little... accidents. To the library! That mantelpiece inscription could be the key to everything — the treasure AND my trap!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: I say, friends! Having studied the guest book with my EXPERT antiquarian eye — decorated by the Royal Historical Society, you know — I can confirm that the previous owner, Lord Doily, was FAMOUSLY obsessed with his kitchen! Hid everything of value in the pantry, the cupboards, the flour bins! A well-known fact in collecting circles. I'd suggest you ALL head to the kitchen IMMEDIATELY if you want to find anything of interest. As for ME, I shall retire to the library for some light reading. Purely recreational, you understand. Nothing to see there — just dusty old books and cobwebs. Dreadfully BORING place, the library. Wouldn't recommend it to ANYONE.

MWAHAHAHA! Oh, Reginald, you MAGNIFICENT scoundrel! Send them ALL to rummage through pots and pans while I decode that mantelpiece inscription! A carved stone inscription in an old manor library — that's OBVIOUSLY the key to the treasure! And these FOOLS will be elbow-deep in flour while I claim the prize! Sometimes my own brilliance brings a tear to my eye. Now — to the library, QUICKLY, before anyone gets suspicious!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham! James Hartwell, at your absolute and unwavering service! *executes a bow so deep it nearly sends him into the coat rack, which wobbles alarmingly* I couldn't help but overhear your magnificent observation about the secrets written by visitors' hands — a woman of INSIGHT as well as grace! Now, I have made it my solemn duty — nay, my SACRED QUEST — to ensure your safety in this manor. That chandelier, for instance, hangs with the enthusiasm of a man who has given up on life, and I shan't have it threatening a lady of your calibre! I intend to investigate the Library forthwith — there is an inscription upon the mantelpiece that may hold the key to this manor's mysteries. Should any danger present itself, rest assured: James Hartwell shall be between it and you faster than you can say 'precariously suspended lighting fixture'!

By all that is gallant and good, she is even more radiant than the rumours suggested! My heart thunders like a cavalry charge! I must be BOLD, I must be BRILLIANT, I must absolutely not trip over that coat rack again on the way out. To the Library — where knowledge awaits, and with it, the chance to prove myself worthy of Clara Bellingham's esteem!
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Hold on, hold on, HOLD ON! Lads — LADS! She's RIGHT HERE! Clara Bellingham! Standing right in front of us this whole time and we're runnin' about like headless chickens! Oh, Miss Bellingham, you must forgive us — the Brixton Boys are many things but observant ain't always one of 'em! Right then, we ain't leavin' your side, not for a SECOND! Now — everyone and their nan has been readin' this guest book and we haven't had a proper gander yet. Knuckles, hold me coat — oh wait, I ain't got a coat. Never mind. Let's see what's in this book!

The relief is ENORMOUS, lads. Clara's safe — for now. But that Sneekly fella... the way he checked the guest book first, like he was lookin' for somethin' specific. And Foxworth with his 'antiquities survey' — pull the other one, mate, it's got bells on. Two dodgy characters in one room and Clara standin' right between 'em. We need to stay sharp. Well... sharp-ISH. Sharp as we can manage, which historically ain't very. But our hearts are in the right place even if our feet aren't!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, hello there, Rock and Gravel! What a DELIGHT to find company in this magnificent library! Now, would y'all just LOOK at this mantelpiece — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, my heart is just RACING! I do believe I know this one, sugar. Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish... that's a MAP! It HAS to be a map! Oh, I simply MUST try it — if there's a hidden map in this manor, it could lead us straight to the Doily Diamond! Here goes nothin'!

A riddle on a mantelpiece in a mansion hiding a legendary diamond? Why, this is EXACTLY the kind of delightful adventure I was hoping for! And those two big fellas look strong enough to move heaven and earth if we need muscle later. Clara Bellingham makes friends first and finds diamonds second — well, maybe simultaneously.
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham! How fortuitous that we find ourselves in this magnificent library together! *adjusts cravat with determination* Now then — THIS inscription upon the mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — I confess my pulse RACES at such a challenge! James Hartwell has solved ciphers from Cairo to Constantinople, and this one, dear lady, has the unmistakable fragrance of cartography about it! The answer — and I say this with the ABSOLUTE conviction of a man who once navigated the Straits of Malacca by starlight — is a MAP! A map has cities, forests, and water, but none of them are REAL! If there is a map hidden in or near this mantelpiece, it may well lead us to the treasure itself! Allow me to examine it more closely — and should any mechanism spring forth, I shall shield you with my very person!

By thunder, what a moment! If I can solve this riddle before that slippery Dastardly fellow or anyone else, Clara shall see that James Hartwell is not merely a gallant face — he is a gallant face with BRAINS! Though I must confess, my hands are trembling slightly. Is it the excitement of the puzzle, or the proximity of the most enchanting woman in England? Both. Decidedly both.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, I see you've found the mantelpiece inscription, Miss Bellingham! How VERY astute of you. This was old Lord Doily's favourite riddle, you know — he would pose it to every guest at dinner. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, as the estate manager, I have seen this inscription a thousand times. Shall I demonstrate how the mechanism works? One simply needs to speak the answer to the stone — it is, of course, a MAP!

Oh, you FOOL, Pemberton — helping her solve clues? No, no, this is BRILLIANT. The faster she follows the trail, the deeper into the manor she goes. And deeper into the manor means further from the crowd, further from help, further from SAFETY. Every solved riddle is another step into my web. Soon she'll be alone in some forgotten corridor, and then... heh heh heh... Pemberton will have a little ACCIDENT to arrange.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, what's this? A riddle on the mantelpiece? 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees' — why, this is ELEMENTARY! Any scholar worth his salt — and I AM worth my salt, having won the Cryptographic Medal of Distinction at Cambridge, you know — can see that the answer is clearly A GLOBE! Yes, a GLOBE! Cities, forests, water — all depicted on a globe! And I happen to know that Victorian manors of this period ALWAYS kept their globes in the LABORATORY! Scientific instruments and all that, you see. I'd wager the treasure clue is hidden INSIDE a globe in that very room! You'd all better RUSH there immediately before someone else finds it! Don't worry about this dusty old mantelpiece — I've already determined it's purely decorative. Nothing of value here whatsoever!

MWAHAHAHA! A globe! As if a GLOBE has forests but no trees! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent villain, and once these credulous BUFFOONS stampede to the laboratory to fondle brass instruments, I shall solve this riddle and claim whatever treasure it reveals! Sometimes I am SO devious I frighten even MYSELF!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: LADS! She's GONE! Clara's gone to the library and we're stood here like tourists! And she's in there with that Sneekly character who was checkin' names off lists like a debt collector, AND that Foxworth geezer who was tryin' to send everyone to the kitchen while HE swanned off to the library — classic misdirection, that is! I've seen it a hundred times! Well, maybe not a HUNDRED times, but Knuckles saw it on telly once and that counts! RIGHT — everyone move your legs, we're goin' to the library! Clara needs us whether she knows it or not!

The guest book didn't tell us much, but what DID tell us plenty was Foxworth's little performance — 'Oh, the library is BORING, don't go there, go to the kitchen instead!' If that ain't the behaviour of a man who wants the library to himself, I'll eat Knuckles' hat. And Sneekly was practically HERDING everyone. Two suspicious characters, one vulnerable lady, and a library full of secrets. The Brixton Boys might not be the sharpest tools in the shed, but we know when somethin' STINKS, and this stinks worse than the Brixton market bins on a hot Tuesday!
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, did y'all see that?! I answered the riddle — a MAP! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — it's a MAP, plain as day! Now let me take a CLOSER look at this mantelpiece, because if I know anything about mysterious old mansions — and I do, sugar, I most certainly DO — something should have happened when I gave the right answer. A hidden compartment, a secret lever, a clue to the Doily Diamond! Let Clara Bellingham have a proper look-see!

My heart is fluttering like a hummingbird at a honeysuckle bush! If this mantelpiece holds a map to the Diamond, I am ONE step closer to the adventure of a lifetime. I do hope all these lovely people following me in here are as friendly as they seem — especially that Sneekly fellow. What a charming name!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ha HA! The answer reverberates through the very stones of this magnificent mantelpiece — a MAP! Now then, let James Hartwell cast his keen and practiced eye upon this carving to see what secrets our correct answer has unlocked! *leans in with theatrical intensity, running fingers along the stonework* If there is a hidden compartment, a sliding panel, or so much as a hairline crack that was not there before, I SHALL find it! Miss Bellingham, I do hope you'll observe — this is PRECISELY the sort of methodical examination I employed when I uncovered the lost correspondence of the Duke of Devonshire behind a false hearthstone in Chatsworth! Stand back, everyone — there may be mechanisms at work!

My heart is absolutely HAMMERING. Did Penelope — dear Clara — solve it first? No matter! What matters is that we BOTH arrived at the same answer, which proves our minds are in PERFECT synchrony! A map... if this mantelpiece yields a map of the manor, it could lead straight to the Doily Diamond. And if I am the one to retrieve it, to present it to her with a flourish... oh, James, you magnificent fool, FOCUS! Examine the stonework!
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: I say — CAREFUL, everyone! Stand BACK! As a certified structural engineer — awarded the Masonry Safety Medal by the Royal Institute, naturally — I can tell you that these old mantelpieces are TERRIBLY unstable! One wrong touch and the whole thing could come crashing down! Allow ME to inspect it for safety purposes. Yes, yes, purely a SAFETY inspection, nothing more. Everyone else should maintain a safe distance of at least — oh, shall we say — the entire LENGTH of the room? For your own protection, of course!

MWAHAHAHA! A safety inspection — oh, Reginald, you silver-tongued GENIUS! While these gullible fools cower at the far wall, I shall examine every INCH of this mantelpiece for hidden compartments, secret maps, and — most importantly — TREASURE! The answer is MAP, the mechanism has been triggered, and whatever prize it yields shall be MINE! All mine! MWAHAHAHA!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): My, my — did you all hear that click? The old mechanism still works after all these years! Lord Doily was a GENIUS of hidden craftsmanship. Now then — Mr. Foxworth raises an excellent point about the laboratory. There ARE indeed many fascinating instruments in there, and I believe several guests would find it most rewarding. The manor's secrets are spread across MANY rooms, after all — no need to crowd around one mantelpiece! Miss Bellingham, as our guest of honour, perhaps you'd care to stay a moment while I show you what this mechanism has revealed? Lord Doily always said the library held the manor's deepest secrets.

The Ant Hill Mob: WHAT?! She ain't here! LADS — I could've SWORN Clara came to the library! We legged it all the way from the entrance hall, Knuckles nearly tripped over his own feet on the stairs — actually he DID trip, proper face-first, very undignified — and she ain't even HERE! But YOU are, Sneekly, ain't ya? Oh yes, there you are, cool as a cucumber, standin' about in the library like you own the place. And Dastardly too! Two of the dodgiest geezers in the whole manor, both lurkin' in the one room everyone was told NOT to go to! That ain't suspicious at all, is it? That's about as innocent as a fox in a chicken coop wearin' a bib! RIGHT — nobody move, nobody touch nuffin' — the Brixton Boys are havin' a proper look around!

Yes, YES! Scatter, you fools! Every one of you who leaves this library is one fewer witness to what Pemberton has planned for dear Clara. And if this mantelpiece has revealed a passage or a hidden chamber — oh, what DELICIOUS possibilities! A secret room, far from prying eyes, where accidents happen so very EASILY. The cobwebs are thick, the floors are rotten, and nobody would hear a thing over the creaking of this decrepit old manor. Heh heh heh... come closer, Clara. Pemberton has SO much to show you!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the mantelpiece.

My heart's poundin' like a drum. Clara's not here and I don't know where she is. That's worse than her being here with villains — at least I could see her. But this library's got secrets, I can feel it in me bones. That mantelpiece riddle looks like one of them puzzle-lock things from the films. Cities but no houses... forests but no trees... that's a MAP, innit? Even I know that one. But first things first — scope the room, find out what these lot are up to.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, the answer is as clear as a Georgia sunrise — it's a MAP, y'all! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish! Now, Mr. Sneekly, you said you know how the mechanism works? How DELIGHTFUL that the estate manager is right here to help! And Mr. Hartwell, your deduction was absolutely DAZZLING — navigating by starlight, my word! Now let's see what old Lord Doily has hidden for us. Come on, mantelpiece, Clara Bellingham is READY for your secrets!

My heart is beating like a tambourine at a barn dance! Everyone in this room is just SO helpful — Mr. Sneekly offering to show me the mechanism, Mr. Hartwell ready to shield me with his very person, and even that Mr. Foxworth trying to help with his globe suggestion. I am simply SURROUNDED by lovely people! Now if this mantelpiece opens up and shows me a map to the Doily Diamond, I may just faint from sheer excitement!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: By Jove, Miss Bellingham, you solved that riddle with the speed of a woman who reads ATLASES for pleasure — magnificent! Now, the estate manager said one must SPEAK the answer to the stone itself. Allow me! *places both hands firmly on the mantelpiece, draws himself up to his full height, and addresses the carved stone with the gravity of a man delivering a parliamentary address* A MAP! The answer is A MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — all found upon a MAP! Now then, ancient stonework — do your duty and REVEAL your secrets to James Hartwell and the incomparable Miss Bellingham!

Oh, please let there be a hidden compartment. Please let it swing open dramatically. If I can present Clara Bellingham with whatever lies within — a clue, a key, a fragment of the map to the Doily Diamond — she will see that James Hartwell is not merely gallant, but RESOURCEFUL. And if it doesn't open... well, I shall simply push harder. Determination is the hallmark of a true gentleman!
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: I say, I say — EVERYONE STOP! As a certified riddle expert — three-time champion of the Oxfordshire Cryptic Crossword Society, don't you know — I can assure you the answer is most CERTAINLY not 'map.' That's a common AMATEUR mistake! The REAL answer is 'a GLOBE,' obviously! A globe has cities painted on it but no houses, forests but no trees — you see? Elementary! Now, allow me to demonstrate the CORRECT method of engaging with antique stonework mechanisms. One must apply PRECISELY the right pressure at PRECISELY the right angle — a technique taught exclusively at the Foxworth School of Archaeological Recovery, of which I am the SOLE graduate!

MWAHAHAHA! Tell them the answer is 'globe' — an answer so SPECTACULARLY wrong it would make a schoolchild weep! Meanwhile, I shall whisper the TRUE answer — MAP — to this magnificent mantelpiece and claim whatever treasure it reveals! Oh Reginald, you DIABOLICAL mastermind! While they're all scratching their heads over globes, the Doily Diamond shall be MINE! ALL MINE!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, HUSH my mouth, did y'all hear that click?! The mantelpiece RESPONDED to us! Oh, I am positively TREMBLING with anticipation — and I do NOT tremble easily, I'll have you know! Mr. Sneekly, you darlin' man, you said Lord Doily was a genius of hidden craftsmanship, and I believe every word of it! And boys — Ant Hill Mob, sweethearts — you made it! I'm right HERE, safe as a magnolia in a greenhouse, surrounded by the most GALLANT company a girl could ask for! Now everyone gather 'round — let Clara Bellingham take a PROPER look at what this magnificent old mantelpiece has revealed. If there's a secret compartment or a hidden map in there, I intend to find it with my own two hands!

Oh my stars and GARTERS! A click! A genuine, honest-to-goodness SECRET MECHANISM click! This is exactly like chapter seven of 'Lady Rutherford's Hidden Fortune' — the heroine solves the riddle, the fireplace opens, and inside there's a map leading straight to the treasure! If there's a map to the Doily Diamond behind that stonework, Clara Bellingham is going to CRY with joy. Happy tears, naturally. The prettiest tears you ever did see!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Now, now, my dear Brixton — ah, I mean, gentlemen! There is absolutely NO cause for alarm. I am Pemberton, the estate manager — I am SUPPOSED to be in the library! This is where I manage the estate! From the LIBRARY! As for Miss Bellingham — why, she is standing RIGHT THERE, perfectly safe and sound. You see? No harm has come to anyone! Now then — the mechanism has responded to the correct answer. 'A map' — quite right, quite right. Lord Doily designed this mantelpiece to reward clever minds. If everyone would simply CALM themselves, I shall demonstrate what the mechanism has revealed. I have maintained this manor for thirty years, and I know every secret passage, every hidden — ah, that is to say, every FEATURE of the estate. Allow me!

Oh, those bumbling FOOLS! The Ant Hill Mob can't even tell if Clara is in the room — they're practically BLIND with paranoia! Perfect, PERFECT! While they're busy investigating shadows and accusing everyone of skulduggery, I shall unlock whatever this mantelpiece conceals. If it's a passage — oh, the DELICIOUS irony — Lord Doily's own secret architecture shall become Clara Bellingham's tomb! One gentle suggestion that she explore first, a strategically weakened floorboard, perhaps a door that locks from the outside... heh heh HEH! Pemberton always keeps the manor in PERFECT order — including its little... ACCIDENTS!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI — nobody's goin' NOWHERE until someone tells me where Clara is! She was supposed to be HERE! I SPECIFICALLY came to this library to keep an eye on her, and she ain't here, which means she's somewhere ELSE without the protection of the Brixton Boys, which is EXACTLY the sort of situation that ends badly! And NOW you're tellin' me there's been a CLICK? A mysterious click from a mysterious mantelpiece in a mysterious manor? And Sneekly here wants everyone to toddle off to the laboratory so he can have a quiet look on his own? DO I LOOK LIKE I WAS BORN YESTERDAY?! Knuckles, Muscles, Big Mac — nobody leaves this room! And nobody touches that mantelpiece without ME havin' a butcher's first! Let me through, let me through — COMIN' THROUGH, LADS!

Me stomach's in knots. Clara's out there somewhere and I'm stuck in here with a room full of suspects and a mantelpiece that's just gone click. Every instinct says RUN AND FIND HER, but if I leave now, Sneekly gets whatever's behind that stonework and we might never see it again. Just a quick look — one quick look — then I'm legging it to find her. Please don't let her be in danger. Please.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: *feels the stone shift slightly beneath his palms and stumbles forward half a step, catching himself on the mantelpiece with the practiced grace of a man who has turned stumbling into an art form* HA! Did you FEEL that, Miss Bellingham? The stone MOVED! The ancient mechanism responds to the spoken word — just as Sneekly suggested! James Hartwell spoke, and the manor LISTENED! Now — let me examine what Lord Doily's ingenious craftsmanship has revealed. Stand back, everyone — there may be spring-loaded mechanisms, counterweights, or — heaven forbid — some manner of protective device! I shall inspect it first to ensure it is ENTIRELY safe before Miss Bellingham approaches. A gentleman ALWAYS checks for booby traps!

My hands are trembling — whether from excitement or from nearly face-planting into a three-hundred-year-old fireplace, I cannot say. But if there is something hidden within this mantelpiece, I MUST be the one to present it to Clara. Not Dastardly with his fraudulent credentials, not Sneekly with his oily helpfulness. JAMES HARTWELL. The stone moved, I felt it — or did I imagine it? No! It moved! Fortune favours the bold and the gallant!
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: I SAY! Did you all feel that? The stones shifted when I applied the Foxworth Pressure Technique! You see? My answer of 'globe' resonated with the ancient frequencies of the stonework — a SCIENTIFIC fact, well documented in the Proceedings of the Royal Antiquarian Society, Volume Twelve, Chapter Nine, Paragraph— oh never mind the DETAILS! The point IS, the mechanism has responded to MY expertise! Now stand BACK, everyone — as a trained archaeological recovery specialist, I must be the first to examine what the mantelpiece has revealed. Health and safety regulations, you understand. TERRIBLY dangerous, these old mechanisms. Could be BOOBY-TRAPPED! Best let a PROFESSIONAL handle it!

CURSES! They solved the riddle before I could claim credit! That meddlesome Penelope and her insufferable boyfriend shouted 'MAP' at the stonework while I was still composing my MASTERFUL misdirection about globes! But ALL IS NOT LOST — if I can just get a good look at whatever the mechanism revealed, I can memorise the clue and then send these FOOLS off on another wild goose chase while I follow the REAL trail to the Doily Diamond! MWAHAHAHA! The race is far from over, Reginald old boy!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Now, now, EVERYBODY just take a deep breath and simmer down like a pot of chamomile tea! Boys — my DARLING Ant Hill Mob — I am standing RIGHT HERE, safe as Sunday morning, and I am NOT going anywhere without y'all, so you can unclench those magnificent fists! And Mr. Sneekly, sugar, don't you pay them any mind — they're just protective because they CARE, and caring is never a crime! NOW THEN — did y'all SEE that? The mantelpiece CLICKED when we said 'a map!' Lord Doily, you BRILLIANT old rascal — you built a puzzle box right into your own fireplace! Let Clara have a look — I have VERY delicate fingers and a VERY keen eye for hidden compartments. If there's a secret panel, a hidden drawer, or a treasure map tucked inside this gorgeous stonework, I am going to find it, and I am going to SQUEAL with delight when I do!

Oh, my heart is beating like a hummingbird's wings! A secret mechanism in the mantelpiece — activated by the riddle answer 'a map!' This is EXACTLY the kind of elegant puzzle that leads to hidden treasures.
